diagnosis.reason: Best allowed A-only design is A=true, B/C/D=false, C_uF=540, R_kohm=45, h=1.0, mass_g=4.65, gate_V=2.11, L2_mm=18, m2_g=0.14, trigger_V=0.55. It passes cold_charge (2.358), burst_energy (0.098), capture (1.207), stress (0.830), area (0.461), rectifier_voltage (0.0038), and acquisition_window (2.281), but fails energy with slack -0.0973: harvested_uW=42.266 versus required_uW=51.998, a 9.73 uW shortfall. Sweeps show the maximum harvestable average power is about 42.3 uW near the 45 Hz background resonance; increasing R to satisfy rectifier voltage lowers harvested power, and the 210 Hz event is too far from the harvester’s tunable resonance to add useful average power. Module A is already the lowest-overhead way to avoid polling (without A/B the required power is ~1876 uW); B adds 180 uW idle, C adds write/idle cost, and D adds idle/shunt loss, so no allowed module can close the deficit. A larger/stronger harvester or lower digital energy/duty cycle is required.

diagnosis.missing_function: Event-band (210 Hz) energy harvesting / a transducer with sufficient power — the design has no way to harvest the event's vibration, and background-only harvesting cannot meet the node's power demand.
diagnosis.reason: The energy constraint is structurally infeasible with the given harvester and module set. Best achievable harvested power is ~42.3 uW (peak at base resonance h=1.0, mass=4.65 g, which is tuned to the 45 Hz / 0.095 g background), while any triggered-capture node (module A on) has required_uW pinned at 51.998 uW — a fixed ~9.7 uW (-0.097) deficit independent of R_kohm, C_uF, gate_V, trigger_V, L2_mm, h, and mass_g (verified across 1D and 2D sweeps). The event (210 Hz, 0.5 g, 150 ms) cannot be harvested: beam resonance scales ~ t^1.5/sqrt(M_tip), and within h in [0.85,1.15] and mass in [3.5,5.8] the resonance only shifts from ~45 Hz to ~65 Hz, so event_voltage never exceeds ~0.085 V across the entire space (vs 2.4 V background resonance). Removing A reverts to polling (required ~1.9 mW+), and B/C/D only add idle power. Burst (needs C >~ 100-670 uF) and rectifier_voltage (needs low gate_V ~1.9-2.0 or high R >~ 90k) are individually tunable but irrelevant because the net energy balance is negative under every legal configuration, so the node would drain storage in ~40 s. Diagnosis: no available tuning of the single harvester can supply the ~52 uW needed for continuous event-triggered acquisition from a 45 Hz background delivering only ~42 uW; a harvester resonant in the event band (210 Hz) with higher output, or a different energy source, would be required. Forcing a design here would only add unnecessary hardware (huge C, extra modules) without passing.

reason: Find exact h for heavy mass (5.6-5.8 g) to resonate at background 45 Hz; power at resonance scales with mass, potentially exceeding the 52 uW energy requirement.

Commit the verified passing design: module A (triggered wake, mandatory since no-wake/B are energy-infeasible), harvester at max tip mass 5.8 g with h=1.075 to keep 45 Hz resonance (peak ~52 uW), R=45.8 for optimal extraction, C=280 uF for burst energy, gate=2.35 V to balance rectifier vs burst/cold-charge. All slacks were non-negative and pass_=true in exploration.
Fine-tune R and h at max mass 5.8 g right at the 45 Hz resonance to maximize harvested-power margin above the 52 uW energy requirement.

Install module A (only viable wake architecture; B excluded by energy). Tune harvester to max-mass 5.8g at h=1.065, R=130 to hit the sharp 45 Hz resonance giving 53.5 uW (>52 required). Set C=220 and gate_V=3.0 to satisfy burst_energy while keeping rectifier_voltage positive, cold_charge and area comfortable. Expect all constraints positive.

Fine-scan the 45 Hz harvester resonance region for a geometry with harvested power above the 52 uW requirement, since coarse sampling showed a very sharp peak near h=1.0, mass=4.65 g.
Add cheap passive trigger (A) to replace polling, increase storage and gate voltage to supply burst energy (255.5 uJ digital). Test if burst/energy resolves.
Very fine scan around the sharp 45 Hz resonance peak to see whether a nearby thickness/mass pair raises harvested power from 42 uW toward the 52 uW requirement.
Lower gate to 2.9V: still ample burst energy with C=470, but reduces the rectified voltage needed, aiming to clear rectifier_voltage while keeping energy/burst pass.

Check whether the wake threshold is causing extra background-triggered acquisitions; raising trigger_V above the 45 Hz background envelope but below the 210 Hz event envelope could reduce required average energy while preserving capture.

Search along the higher-mass/lower-frequency side of the 45 Hz resonance ridge (h above 1.0 with compensating tip mass) for a higher-power operating point, since the constant-frequency ridge may raise power while staying at 45 Hz.
At the higher-mass resonance-ridge point h=1.06/mass=5.8 g, sweep load resistance because the optimal electrical damping may shift and could raise harvested power above 52 uW.
At maximum tip mass 5.8 g, jointly tune thickness and load resistance to maximize harvested power and create margin above the 51.998 uW requirement while keeping stress/area acceptable.
Fine-tune thickness and load near the h≈1.06/R≈110 kΩ ridge point (already 52.2 uW) to maximize harvested-power margin above the fixed 51.998 uW requirement.

Isolate the rectifier_voltage failure: keep C=100 but restore gate_V to the value that previously passed the rectifier. This tells whether the rectifier issue was driven by gate_V (not storage), and whether C=100 at gate 2.9 already meets the burst budget.
At the energy-positive harvester point, size storage and MCU start threshold for sufficient burst energy and cold-charge/rectifier margin without unnecessary area.
Fine-search the ridge maximum to increase the very tight energy slack (currently only +0.98 uW) while retaining positive rectifier and stress margins.
Final micro-tune of the narrow resonance ridge around h=1.06 and R=150 kΩ to see if energy margin can be increased beyond +0.98 uW before committing.
The energy slack improved at h=1.062; continue along the ridge to locate the peak and maximize margin before committing the design.
Commit the energy-positive harvester ridge point (h=1.062, tip mass=5.8 g, R=135 kΩ) with A-only wake and 200 uF/2.8 V storage/gate for sufficient burst energy and cold-charge margin.
Enable triggered acquisition (A) and tune both the harvester beam (thin/short-mass for ~210 Hz) and trigger beam to the event frequency; lower gate to ease charging.

Hypothesis: rectifier_voltage is an LDO-dropout rule, V_rectified >= gate_V + bridge drop (~0.3). At gate 2.9/3.2 it needs more than the harvester's ~few-volt rectified output can provide, so it fails regardless. Lowering gate to 2.4 keeps burst energy ample (C=470 gives ~590 uJ) while reducing the required rectified voltage.

Data shows rectifier_voltage is driven by storage size (C=75 passes, C=100 fails) not by the MCU threshold. Burst needs 0.5*C*(gate^2-1.8^2) >= digital 255.5 uJ; at gate 3.2 the max allowed, C=80 gives ~280 uJ (10% margin) while staying close to the known-good C=75 for the rectifier, and charge energy (~410 uJ) is well under the ~512 uJ already shown to charge in time.

Key insight: the initial C=75 design did NOT flag rectifier_voltage (it flagged energy), so the harvester's rectified voltage/timing is fine at small C. The rectifier_voltage fault appeared only after enlarging C to 470 — an oversized cap can't be charged by the limited rectified output fast enough. Shrink storage to ~150 uF (still gives ~390 uJ usable, enough for the ~255-300 uJ burst) while keeping gate 2.9 and passive trigger A.

Re-architect: harvest background 45 Hz continuously for cold-charge/sustained power (heavy mass, thin beam -> low resonance), while trigger beam A stays tuned high (~210 Hz) for event wake. Larger storage for burst margin above brownout.

Rectifier failures track storage size: C=75 passed, C=80 (this gate) and C=100 both failed. So C must stay just above the base value. Burst needs 0.5*C*(3.2^2-1.8^2) >= 255.5 uJ -> C>=73; C=76 gives ~266 uJ (margin) while remaining only 1 uF above the known-good rectifier point. Gate 3.2 is required for feasibility because with C<80 the higher threshold is needed to reach the burst energy. Charge energy ~389 uJ is under the ~512 uJ already shown to charge within 100 s, area is ~37 mm2, and A/triggered capture, stress, and energy were already passing.

Keep harvester tuned low (~background 45 Hz) for cold-charge power, but shrink C (300 uF) and raise gate to 2.3 V to cut the R*C charge time while still keeping usable burst energy above brownout (0.5*C*(2.3^2-1.8^2)≈308 uJ > 255.5 uJ).

Enable passive tuned trigger comparator A. Bounds show polling-only needs ~2144 uW and B-based wake needs ~180 uW idle, both above the ~74 uW harvest ceiling, so A is the only viable wake scheme. Keep other parameters at baseline to observe detailed feedback.

rectifier_voltage is invariant to gate (2.4/2.9/3.2 all fail) and to storage size, so it is a high-voltage/surge magnitude problem, not a dropout/undervoltage one. That matches the environment's dedicated mitigation: module D, a voltage-triggered shunt for "high observed voltage" that also limits beam stress. Clamp just above the ~3 V operating point (shield 5 V) with a low shunt resistance to keep the event-driven rectified spikes within rectifier/stress limits, while keeping A (trigger), C=150 uF (burst) and gate 2.9 V.

Usable burst energy = 0.5*C*(gate_V^2 - 1.8^2). At 75uF/2.9V it's ~194uJ < 255.5uJ needed. With C=250uF and gate 3.0V it's ~720uJ, ample margin, while charging to 3.0V needs only ~11uW average over 100s (area cost 7.5mm2, still within 95mm2).
Analytic bound shows no-wake and B-only architectures are energy-excluded; A is required. Enable A first to obtain full constraint diagnostics.

Gate 3.0V tripped the rectifier voltage constraint (0.3V bridge drop makes that threshold unattainable). Reverting to 2.9V. Burst is still satisfied by C=250uF: 0.5*250uF*(2.9^2-1.8^2)=646uJ >> 255.5uJ, so storage not gate threshold provides burst headroom.
Burst energy ½C(gate²−1.8²) must exceed ~255.5µJ/0.85≈300µJ. With C=120, gate 3.0 that is 346µJ (good margin) while stored energy stays modest to preserve charging within ready_s.

Lower gate to 2.1 V so the background-driven rectified voltage (V≈sqrt(P·R)≈2.4 V) actually exceeds the start threshold (fixing cold-charge reach), while C=450 uF keeps burst energy above brownout (≈0.5·450e-6·(2.1²−1.8²)≈263 uJ > 255.5 uJ) with a modest R·C charge time.

Rectifier voltage is set by the load, not the gate. For a current-source-driven rectifier, a larger equivalent input load R raises the rectified DC voltage so it can clear the bridge drop and reach the regulation threshold. Raising R from 45 to 120 kohm; C=250uF/gate 2.9V keep burst satisfied.

Minimal, robust change from a known starting point: add A (triggered acquisition removes polling cost, fixing the original energy/capture failure) while keeping the harvester near its base tuning that already gave reasonable cold-charge, tune the trigger beam up to the 210 Hz event, and size C=400 uF / gate 2.2 V for burst margin (≈320 uJ above brownout).

Cold-charge now clears (capture is the worst constraint). The wake trigger is failing to fire within the 150 ms event; lowering the wake-envelope threshold to 0.2 V makes the tuned trigger beam detect the 210 Hz event reliably (and it still ignores the weak 45 Hz background), so the 62.5 ms acquisition lands inside the event window.

Resonance must track the 210Hz event to raise V_oc so the rectified voltage clears the bridge drop at the power-optimal load. f ~ h^1.5/sqrt(m): base->h=1.15,m=3.5 gives ~1.42x, matching a base resonance near 148Hz up to 210Hz. This is also the min-damping corner (c=2*zeta*sqrt(km)) maximizing harvested power, and R back near 1/(omega*Cp)~40k where the energy budget already passed. C=250uF/gate 2.9 keeps burst (646uJ) and area (42.5mm2) satisfied.

Reduce storage from 250uF to 120uF to fix cold_charge: charging energy to 2.9V falls from ~1051uJ to ~504uJ (roughly halves charge time within the 100s window). Burst still covered: 0.5*120uF*(2.9^2-1.8^2)=310uJ > 255.5uJ. Area = 20 + 120*0.03 + 15(A) = 38.6mm2 < 95. Only module A is installed (B too power-hungry, C unnecessary, D would waste harvested power).
Capture full feedback/flags for the initial design before changing anything.

Enable the passive trigger beam A (only energy-feasible wake architecture per analytic bound: active_A ~52uW < 74uW harvest ceiling, while no-wake polling ~2144uW and module B ~231uW are excluded). Keep everything else at initial to read the full per-constraint slack report.

Burst_energy failed because C=75uF/gate 2.9V gives only ~194uJ usable vs 255.5uJ needed. Raise C to 320uF and gate to 2.5V: usable above brownout = 0.5*320uF*(2.5^2-1.8^2)=0.5*320e-6*3.01=482uJ (>255.5uj, good margin). Charge energy 0.5*320uF*2.5^2=1000uJ, achievable well within 100s ready window at tens of uW. Area impact modest (0.03*320=9.6mm2).

Lower gate_V to 2.7 so rectified DC (−bridge/regulator drops) clears the start threshold. Raise C to 155 so burst energy ½·155µ·(2.7²−1.8²)=314µJ still exceeds ~300µJ; stored ½·155µ·2.7²=565µJ stays near the charging-safe level.
Locate harvester resonance vs event with triggered acquisition enabled and large storage to isolate energy.
Map storage vs gate threshold effect on burst/charging energy headroom.

rectifier_voltage fails: the rectified voltage likely cannot reach/maintain gate_V=2.5V. Raising R (lighter regulator load) lifts the rectified voltage and reduces electrical damping/voltage sag. Lowering gate slightly to 2.45V gives startup margin. Burst check: 0.5*320uF*(2.45^2-1.8^2)=0.5*320e-6*2.7625=442uJ >255.5uJ still OK; charge energy 0.5*320uF*2.45^2=960uJ fine within 100s.

Rectifier bus voltage V=I·|R∥(1/jωC_p)| rises with the equivalent input load R toward V_oc. At R=45kΩ the heavy load depresses the bus; raising R to 120kΩ lifts the rectified voltage to clear gate_V+drops while (if below power-match) also aiding charging.
Find storage/gate window where burst_energy and cold_charge both hold at default beam.

Resolve the R power/voltage trade-off by keeping R low for harvest power (R=50, near the energy-OK 45) but lowering gate_V to 1.95V so the rectified voltage easily exceeds the startup threshold (fixes rectifier_voltage). Compensate the smaller usable-voltage window with a larger reservoir C=1100uF: burst usable=0.5*1100uF*(1.95^2-1.8^2)=309uJ>255.5uJ, and after the 255.5uJ acquisition V_end=sqrt(2*54uJ/1100uF+1.8^2)=1.83V (stays above 1.8 brownout). Charge energy 0.5*1100uF*1.95^2=2091uJ, well within 100s. Area=20+33+15=68mm2 (<95).

Check whether higher load R and higher thickness improve average energy constraint.

Energy failures only occurred with R>45 (R=50 and R=120 starve power below the ~52uW active-A floor). Revert R to 45 to restore harvest power. Keep gate_V low at 1.95V (V at R=45 is below 2.5 but should exceed ~2V) so the rectifier can reach the start threshold (fixes rectifier_voltage). Size C=1000uF for burst at gate 1.95: usable=0.5*1000uF*(1.95^2-1.8^2)=281uJ>255.5uJ; V_end after burst=sqrt(2*25.5uJ/1000uF+1.8^2)=1.825V (above 1.8 brownout). Charge energy 0.5*1000uF*1.95^2=1901uJ -> ~37s at 52uW (<100s ready). Area=20+30+15=65mm2<95.

Compare the no-module-A fast-polling acquisition branch for energy consumption.

Mass-controlled harvester: bus V saturates near I/(ωC_p), power ∝ V²/R. Thicker PZT (h=1.15) raises V_oc/V for the same strain; R=60kΩ stays near voltage saturation (~93%) but delivers ~2× the power of R=120kΩ. This should keep the bus above gate_V+drops (rectifier) while lifting harvested power above consumption (energy).
Raise thickness for energy margin, lower gate to satisfy cold_charge, larger C for burst at low gate; trigger tuned to event.

Energy = charging-time limited (E_charge/P<=ready_s); the (C=320,gate=2.5) case passed with E_charge=half*C*Vg^2=1000uJ, so keeping E_charge<1000uJ at the same R=45 guarantees the energy constraint passes. Simultaneously burst needs half*C*(Vg^2-1.8^2)>=255.5uJ. These two force Vg>=~2.09V. Chosen Vg=2.13V, C=440uF: E_charge=half*440uF*2.13^2=998uJ (<1000, energy passes), burst usable=half*440uF*(2.13^2-1.8^2)=285uJ (>255.5, 30uJ margin), post-burst voltage=sqrt(2*29.5uJ/440uF+1.8^2)=1.84V (38mV above brownout). R=45 keeps harvest power near its max (energy failures only appeared at R>=50). gate_V is the lowest feasible, giving maximum rectifier-voltage headroom (fixing rectifier_voltage if the sustainable rectified voltage is ~2.2-2.4V). Area=20+13.2+15=48mm2<95; only module A installed (no unnecessary B/C/D).

cold_charge passes at high R (R=120,h=1.0) but fails at R=60. Energy passes at R=60 with h=1.15 due to large coupling margin. Move R up to 80 kΩ: restores cold-charge/startup behavior (raised bus voltage & lighter load draw) while h=1.15 keeps event power above consumption; rectifier stays satisfied by the high saturated bus.

Fine tune beam thickness and tip mass near baseline to locate the resonance peak (max harvested voltage/power) needed to clear both burst energy and charge constraints.

Install passive tuned trigger beam + comparator (module A) to replace polling with triggered acquisition; analytic bound says A-based architecture is the only one whose required power (~52 uW) fits under the harvest ceiling (~74 uW).
